# Atomik Rack keyboard reference

<!-- Generated by `atomik --print-keymap`; do not edit. A test keeps this file equal to the output. -->

Chords are shown as the menus show them. `Ctrl` is the Control key; on macOS the primary modifier is `Cmd` (Command) and Alt is `Opt` (Option), and Control and Command are never interchanged. `Numpad` keys are told apart from the main keys. Letters are matched by the character they type, so a layout that moves a letter moves the shortcut with it; any binding can be changed in Settings, Keyboard (saved as `keymap.json` next to `settings.json`, only your changes). While a text field has focus only chords with the primary modifier, function keys and Esc run commands. Where a binding in a pane overlaps a global one, the pane wins inside that pane. The file browser panel (View, File Browser, `F9`) is the `files` context: while it has the focus, its keys (arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End, Enter, Space, Esc, Backspace, `F`, the search and select-all chords) are the `files.*` commands, which the shell hands to the panel as those keys, so they win over the global bindings of the same chords (Space previews instead of playing, Backspace goes up a folder instead of deleting); every other chord, `F9` and `F5` included, still runs as usual. While the panel's search or tag field has focus, only Esc, function keys and the chords with the primary modifier run commands. The Piano Keys strip (View, Piano Keys, `F4`) plays the computer keyboard while it has the focus in Keys mode: it is the `keys` context, where letters are notes (two rows from `A`, `W`, `S`, `E`... to the F above the next C) and `Z` and `X` change the octave, `1` to `0` set the velocity, and Shift is the sustain pedal (it does not change which key a letter is); a chord the context does not bind, `Space` or any chord with the primary modifier included, still runs as usual. An open menu (a context menu, or a menu of the in-window menu bar) takes every key: Up and Down move the highlight (it wraps, and skips separators and disabled items), Home and End jump to the first and last item, Right or Enter opens a submenu on its first item, Left or Esc closes it (Esc on the first panel closes the menu), Enter or Space chooses, and in the menu bar Left and Right move to the neighbouring menu (Right on an item too).

## Pointer gestures: playhead, locators and markers

| Gesture | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Press and drag | Arrangement ruler | Locates the snapped position under the pointer and keeps locating while the pointer moves (not before zero) |
| Drag the playhead | Arrangement (ruler flag, or its line in the grid) and piano roll (its line in the grid, or the ruler) | Moves the playhead by the distance dragged, snapped |
| Drag the L or R flag | Arrangement ruler, lower band | Moves the left or the right locator, snapped, with one snap step left between them; the loop is set on release (Escape cancels) |
| `Ctrl+click` (`Alt+click` on macOS) | Arrangement ruler | Sets the left locator (the loop start) to the snapped position |
| `Alt+click` (`Cmd+click` on macOS) | Arrangement ruler | Sets the right locator (the loop end) to the snapped position |
| `Shift+click` | Arrangement ruler | Sets the End marker to the snapped position |
| Drag a marker line | Arrangement grid, while the marker strip is shown | Moves the marker, as dragging its label in the strip does |
| `Ctrl+Alt` held | While dragging any of these | No snap |

The locator clicks win over the razor in the ruler. In the grid the playhead and the marker lines are grabbed within three pixels of the line, with the Select tool, without Shift or `Ctrl` held, and never over the edge, fade, point or mute controls of a clip or a note; elsewhere the press does what it did before.

## Pointer gestures: values

| Gesture | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Press and drag up or down | Transport bar, BPM | Changes the field under the pointer live, 5 pixels per step: 1 BPM on the whole part (0.1 with `Shift`), 0.01 on the two decimals; the whole drag is one undo step |
| Mouse wheel | Transport bar, BPM | One notch is one step of the field under the pointer, as for the drag |
| Press and drag up or down | Transport bar, time signature | Steps the beats per bar (1 to 32) on the left of the slash or the beat unit (2, 4, 8, 16) on the right; one undo step per drag |
| Mouse wheel | Transport bar, time signature | One notch is one step of the field under the pointer |
| Press and drag up or down | Snap selector of the arrangement and the piano roll | Steps through the resolutions in the order of the selector, 5 pixels per step, no wrap; a click without movement still cycles forward on release, a right click back |
| Mouse wheel | Snap selector of the arrangement and the piano roll | One notch is one resolution |
| Press and drag up or down, mouse wheel | A value of the quantize, Audio to Notes, Strip Silence and Warp panels (every row with a - and + button) | Steps the value, 5 pixels or one notch per step |
| Double-click | Transport bar, BPM or time signature | Types the value (Enter commits, Esc cancels) |

Up increases and down decreases, and a value stops at the end of its range.

## Modifier roles

A role is a modifier held during a pointer gesture, not a chord. Settings, Keyboard lists the roles that a gesture acts on, and remapping one changes that gesture at once. A role is told apart from the others of its gesture by the exact modifiers held (`Alt` alone and `Ctrl+Alt` are different holds).

| Role | Other systems | macOS | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alternate tool | `Alt` | `Ctrl` | The pointer acts with the alternate tool while held |
| Disable snap | `Ctrl+Alt` | `Cmd+Opt` | No snap while dragging |
| Copy while dragging | `Ctrl` | `Opt` | Dragging clips in the arrangement drops a copy |
| Toggle selection | `Ctrl` | `Cmd` | A click adds the item to the selection or takes it out |
| Range select | `Shift` | `Shift` | A click selects from the last clicked item to this one |
| Fine adjust | `Shift` | `Shift` | A drag or a wheel notch on a knob or fader in the rack and the mixer moves a tenth as far |
| Reset parameter | `Ctrl` | `Cmd` | A click on a knob or fader in the rack and the mixer sets its default (a double-click does too) |

Constrain is a role in the keymap but no gesture reads it yet, so Settings does not list it; a remap of it that is already in `keymap.json` is kept. The places that take a finer step from the modifier on their own (the clip inspector, the macro and plugin panels, the container editor) still use `Shift`.

Many European keyboard layouts report AltGr as `Ctrl+Alt` (the default of Disable snap outside macOS): typing a character with AltGr while dragging switches snapping off. Remap Disable snap in Settings, Keyboard if that gets in the way.

## Tooltips

Resting the pointer on a button for about 0.6 seconds shows a one-line tooltip under it that says what the button does, with the shortcut of its command when it has one (printed as the menus print it, so a key you rebind in Settings, Keyboard shows at once). The tooltip hides on a press, a key, the wheel, or when the pointer leaves the button. Settings, Workflow, **Show tooltips** (on by default) switches them off; the value readout shown while a knob or fader is dragged stays.
